FAST

NAGASAKI, Japan, Nov 12 : Dovish Bank of Japan policymaker Toichiro Asada pushed back against calls within the board for a near-term interest rate hike, arguing on Thursday that premature rate hikes could hurt growth and push down underlying inflation. While an overshoot of inflation above the BOJ's 2 per cent target could have adverse effects on the economy, there was also a risk the effect of past and future rate hikes may weigh on economic activity and underlying inflation, Asada said in a speech to business leaders in Nagasaki, southern Japan. Welcoming data showing real wages turned positive since the turn of 2026, Asada said growth and consumption have lacked momentum. "I believe the recent price increases have not necessarily been driven by demand factors," said Asada, who dissented on the BOJ's decisions to raise interest rates in June and September. "In this sense, I consider it necessary for the Bank to give due consideration to the pace of any policy rate hikes," he said, stressing the need to avoid cooling growth with too-fast rate hikes.

Source: Reuters

SEOUL, Nov 12 : South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Thursday that Samsung Electronics' 6 trillion won ($4.48 billion) investment in a high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chip packaging plant in Asan, South Korea, would be followed by about 40 trillion won in investment in advanced equipment. Lee made the comment during a groundbreaking ceremony for part of the investment plans that Samsung affiliates announced in July. Samsung Electronics said in a presentation that the new HBM production line is scheduled to begin operations in June 2028, a year earlier than initially planned, as the company seeks to meet rapidly growing demand for server memory. The new HBM plant will have three floors of clean-room space covering about 31,000 square metres (37,076 square yards), Samsung said. South Korea's government has tapped Samsung, fellow chipmaker SK Hynix and other companies to help drive "mega projects" covering semiconductors, physical artificial intelligence and AI data centres. ($1 = 1,339.5500 won)

FAST

SEOUL, Nov 12 : Stock brokerage Samsung Securities has found brand ambassadors who never skip rehearsal and are unlikely to make tabloid headlines: a four-member, AI-generated K-pop girl group called LUMINA.  The band's debut music video, "Override", passed 3 million YouTube views about five weeks after release.  Finding presenters for its social media channels was hard, said Uhm Sewon, head of the brokerage's media strategy team. Staff experts were novices on camera, while celebrities were costly and might not suit the brand.  "We make about 1,500 pieces of content a year, and finding people to appear in them is really not easy," Uhm told Reuters.

Beyond human planning, Samsung Securities' team made the song, characters and video all with AI. Rapidly improving tools have made LUMINA's dance moves look far more natural, Uhm said.  Samsung Securities has not registered copyright in the song, and as a brokerage is not registered to earn revenue from music, Uhm said. Under South Korean government guidelines, music generated entirely by AI with no human creative input cannot be registered for copyright. To maintain investors' trust, Samsung Securities labels the characters as "fictional" in prominent block letters, and has finance-related content checked by in-house specialists in about three stages.  "We make clear that they are AI characters, and we produce content only from material that internal experts have verified for accuracy," Uhm said.  Comments below the music video range from "This song is addictive" and "Why is this so natural" to "This beats actual idol groups".  Uhm said it was difficult to quantify measurable returns for its securities business yet, because it was LUMINA's first music video. She said previous Samsung Securities content that combined customer events with YouTube videos attracted more visitors than standalone events, suggesting there would be a positive impact over the longer term.  Next up are a performance video, a follow-up song, member interviews, short-form challenges, investor education videos hosted by the group, and glimpses of the members' daily lives, Uhm said.  AN UNSTOPPABLE TREND Park Sang-cheol, chairman of the Korea Singers Association and a veteran performer, said AI was an unstoppable trend and could benefit artists by cutting production costs and helping singers practise new songs.  However, he warned that AI could hit corporate modelling work, session musicians, songwriters and arrangers hard, with AI-generated likenesses and mass-uploaded AI songs a threat to creators' rights. Park said there was a need to monitor developments closely and put policy safeguards in place. "AI music sounds really good at first, but it has a colour of its own, and the more you listen, the more tiresome it gets," he told Reuters. "That's why live performance has its own flavour – a singer's own colour, even the mistakes. Hearing exactly the same music every single time can become irritating. A singer can talk to the audience, put on events and interact with them, and I don't think AI can replace that." South Korea ranked 12th in the world in generative AI use, posting the largest quarterly increase among major economies for the third consecutive time, according to Microsoft's AI Economy Institute in September.  Virtual K-pop is not new. In 2023, Netmarble's affiliate launched girl band MAVE:, made up of four virtual avatars, with voices provided by human performers. Virtual boy band PLAVE is portrayed by human performers in real time through motion capture.  However, Samsung Securities' LUMINA is entirely AI-generated.   AI is already gatecrashing South Korean music charts. "The Adult I Dreamed Of" by MEOMURU topped multiple South Korean music charts in September and October. A human wrote the lyrics and directed production, but the vocals were generated with the AI program Suno.

Source: Reuters

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 11 : JetBlue Airways' President Marty St. George said on Wednesday that he understands why airlines may be wary of artificial intelligence-powered booking intermediaries, after United Airlines said it would restrict AI bots' access to its digital platforms. United cited data security concerns in its move to block bots, one of the airline industry's clearest signs of resistance to AI agents that are increasingly capable of planning and booking trips on travelers' behalf. St. George said he fears that one day intermediaries could eventually seek compensation for directing bookings, creating a new cost for airlines in an industry where profitability remains elusive. "I can see why the concept of an intermediary may be intimidating for a lot of people," St. George said at the Skift Commerce Summit in New York on Wednesday, adding that the AI industry is likely to attract "a trillion dollars of capital" and "someone's going to have to pay for that."

"That's money we're not spending today. And again, unprofitable company, unprofitable industry, that's intimidating," he said. JetBlue, which has about $8.4 billion in debt and finance lease obligations, has not posted an annual profit since 2019. United said customers who share account credentials with third-party AI assistants could expose sensitive information and risk unintended purchases, account modifications or unauthorized use of frequent-flyer miles. Despite those concerns, St. George said airlines should adapt if customers embrace AI-based booking tools. "We should be responsive to what customers want," he said. "If customers really think that's a better way to do it, we need to figure out how to meet them where they are." St. George said JetBlue also prefers maintaining direct relationships with customers because it allows the carrier to better market the full range of its products. He drew parallels with online travel agencies, which he described as another distribution channel that carries costs for airlines and isn't always beneficial. "It's a channel that has a cost, which jetblue.com does not," he said.

TOKYO, Nov 12 : Japan's top currency diplomat Atsushi Mimura on Thursday warned market participants that it's "too early to forget" this summer's intervention as the yen again edged towards the key 160-per-dollar level. In his first remarks on foreign exchange since late September, Mimura said he believed that recent currency moves have been excessively rapid. "It's still too early to forget what happened this summer," he added, referring to Japan's yen-buying interventions in late July through early August, including one conducted jointly with the US. The dollar rose to 159.94 against the Japanese yen early Thursday morning, hitting its strongest in over two months, buoyed by growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates after hot US inflation data and hawkish remarks from policymakers.

China's Alibaba Group said on Tuesday (Nov 10) its chip unit T-Head had confidentially filed for a Hong Kong initial public offering, advancing a spin-off that would give investors direct exposure to one of the group's key artificial intelligence and chip assets. Alibaba said T-Head submitted a confidential Form A1 application on Sep 11 after the Hong Kong Stock Exchange cleared the Chinese e-commerce giant to proceed with the proposed spin-off. The size of the deal, offering structure and Alibaba's post-listing stake have yet to be determined, the company added. Alibaba said the spin-off would allow investors to better value T-Head and its core businesses separately while helping the chipmaker raise capital independently and strengthen ties with customers, suppliers and strategic partners.

Founded in 2018, T-Head sits at the centre of Alibaba's push to build in-house AI and computing capabilities as Chinese technology firms race to meet rising demand for AI infrastructure and reduce reliance on Nvidia's AI processors amid US export restrictions. The listing would give investors exposure to a business that has become increasingly strategic to Alibaba's ambitions in cloud computing and artificial intelligence. In September, the company unveiled T-Head's Zhenwu V900 AI processor, which it said delivers three times the performance of its previous-generation chip and would underpin training and inference for next-generation AI models. TOKYO, Nov 12 : The dollar climbed to a 19-month high against major peers on Thursday, supported by growing expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike, while the yen edged toward the key 160-per-dollar level following a dovish central banker's speech. Traders ramped up bets on further Fed tightening after stronger-than-expected October inflation data and a series of hawkish remarks from US central bank officials, who expressed concern over stubborn inflation and left open the possibility of a larger 50-basis-point increase. Some major brokerages, including Goldman Sachs, now expect another hike early next year, in addition to one in December. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose by 0.15 per cent to 103.02, the highest since April 2025.

New York Fed President John Williams is set to appear on a panel late Thursday that will be closely watched given his "pre-October FOMC meeting views the Fed had time on rate hikes," said Gavin Friend, senior markets strategist at National Australia Bank, in a note. "Fast forward two weeks and following a hotter-than-forecast October CPI report, Fed officials appear to be falling over themselves to talk up rate hikes," Friend said. "Any guidance from Williams will be seized on." Against the Japanese yen, the dollar reversed an earlier decline to trade 0.04 per cent higher at 159.83, underpinned by wide interest-rate differentials as traders increased bets on further Fed hikes. It hit a more than two-month high earlier on Thursday. Bank of Japan board member Toichiro Asada, one of two dovish policymakers who dissented from September's decision to increase borrowing costs to 1.25 per cent, pushed back against calls within the board for a near-term interest rate hike, saying in a speech that premature rate hikes could hurt growth and push down underlying inflation. Earlier a warning from Japan's top currency diplomat Atsushi Mimura that it was "too early to forget" intervention by Japanese authorities during the summer pushed the dollar/yen pair to its lowest point of the day but the respite for the yen was brief. "Once dollar/yen rises above 160, I think caution will increase another notch," said Sho Suzuki, market analyst at Matsui Securities. "For it to move higher from there, the dollar would need to strengthen further, for example, through a further rise in expectations for Fed rate hikes, or a drop-off in expectations for BOJ rate hikes. Without something like that, the pair may lack enough momentum to test a break above 160," he said. Many analysts in a Reuters poll expect the next BOJ rate hike as soon as next month. That view was strengthened on Thursday by data that showed Japan's annual wholesale inflation re-accelerated to 7.1 per cent in the year to October, up from a 6.8 per cent annual increase in September. The euro was up 0.06 per cent against the US dollar at $1.1096 while sterling slipped 0.1 per cent to $1.3266. The Australian dollar  was little changed versus the greenback at $0.6847, while New Zealand's kiwi was down 0.05 per cent at $0.5559.   In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 0.63 per cent to $73,848.24. Nov 11 : Polymarket has cut jobs and terminated several contractor agreements in a reorganization as the prediction market startup seeks to compete with rapidly growing rival Kalshi. An internal email from the company, ending a contractor agreement, has been doing the rounds on social media platform X since last week. The company confirmed on Wednesday that the email screenshot was genuine. Once the market leader, Polymarket now trails Kalshi in monthly trading volume. The rival prediction market has benefited from expanded distribution and partnerships, including a lucrative deal for the FIFA World Cup. Polymarket declined to disclose the percentage of total workforce affected. Over 50 per cent of the cuts were contractors, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters.

Polymarket named veteran finance executive Warren Jenson as its first chief financial officer in September. NEW YORK/MILAN, Nov 11 : Major stock indexes rose on Wednesday, led by gains in technology shares after an upbeat report from CoreWeave lifted optimism about the AI trade, and the dollar strengthened.  Shares of Nvidia gained 2.9 per cent, recovering some of their recent sharp losses, but the stock fell 8 per cent after the bell after the Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported Nvidia's board was preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 each ended the regular session more than 1 per cent higher, and the S&P 500 technology sector was up 2.7 per cent. Tech shares had been sold off in the wake of the US midterm elections last week amid worries about increased AI regulation and the sustainability of the AI rally. CoreWeave shares finished up 24.7 per cent on Wednesday. The company said it expected to become profitable in 2028, easing concerns that demand may not be strong enough to support its debt-fueled expansion.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe rose 12.41 points, or 1.12 per cent, to 1,121.15. OIL, DOLLAR CLIMB Oil prices rose after the Iranian security chief said Tehran would not allow any enriched nuclear material to leave the country. Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the war between the two countries. Brent futures climbed $1.27, or 1.39 per cent, to settle at $92.76, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 49 cents, or 0.57 per cent, to $86.53. The dollar gained again on Wednesday. Hotter-than-expected US inflation data on Tuesday cemented expectations for an interest rate hike from the Fed next month. Recent hawkish rhetoric from Fed officials added to the view. Traders see a rate hike next month as a certainty, with a roughly 11 per cent chance of a half-percentage-point increase, according to the CME FedWatch tool.  The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.7 per cent to 102.92, with the euro down 0.68 per cent at $1.1087. TOKYO, Nov 12 : One-third of Japanese firms have been hit by cyberattacks targeting either their own systems or those of external service providers this year, a Reuters survey showed on Thursday, prompting companies to ramp up spending on cybersecurity. The findings come after a series of major customer data breaches over recent months prompted the government last week to draw up an emergency package of countermeasures. About 10 per cent of respondents said cyberattacks on their systems or those of their service providers had disrupted operations, while 22 per cent reported cyberattacks that caused no damage. Just over half said they had not been targeted, with the remainder unsure. On cybersecurity spending, 3 per cent foresee a sharp increase, 59 per cent expect a moderate increase and 22 per cent anticipate little change.

"It is an endless battle. But we want to invest as much as possible to step up our security," a manager at a textile company wrote in the survey. Among the surveyed companies, 63 per cent strengthened employee training and anti-phishing steps, 32 per cent stepped up ransomware countermeasures and data backups, and 22 per cent introduced stricter information management. Respondents could select multiple measures, so the figures do not add up to 100 per cent. "It is difficult to achieve perfect protection against AI-driven attacks. We consider it important to implement measures aimed at minimizing the damage should such an attack occur," an official at a chemical company said. Experts say AI is helping automate tasks ranging from scanning for software vulnerabilities to crafting phishing campaigns, making cybercrime faster, cheaper and harder to detect. The poll was conducted by Nikkei Research for Reuters from October 27 to November 6. Nikkei Research contacted 508 companies, of which 214 responded on the condition of anonymity. PAY RISES TO CONTINUE On wage hikes for 2027, more than 80 per cent of respondents said they expect to raise wages at roughly the same pace as in 2026. Rengo, Japan's largest labour union umbrella group with seven million members, said in July that companies agreed to raise wages by an average 5.01 per cent this year, topping the 5 per cent mark for a third straight year amid persistent labour shortages. "If pay hikes are not keeping up with rising prices, top talent will leave us," a manager at a transportation equipment maker said. Several companies in the survey, however, voiced concerns over the sustainability of the current pace of wage increases. "Wage hikes have continued at a rate of around 5 per cent over the past few years, but we are getting closer to the limit of our ability to maintain such a pace," an official at a retailer said. Asked how much they expect to raise wages next year, nearly half of respondents chose 3 per cent-5 per cent, one-third selected 1 per cent-3 per cent and 12 per cent picked 5 per cent-7 per cent.

FAST

SYDNEY, Nov 12 : Australia's blue-chip companies are increasingly invoking artificial intelligence as they cut jobs and move work offshore, unions and experts say, complicating the government's efforts to support employment in a slowing economy. On Tuesday, Qantas, Australia's flag carrier, said it would cut 850 jobs and outsource some corporate functions offshore as part of an AI-driven overhaul with consulting firm Accenture, a move that has raised accusations of "AI washing." "AI washing" describes a practice by companies of attributing layoffs to AI tools when the primary driver may be broader cost-cutting measures, such as shifting jobs offshore. Tech companies WiseTech and Atlassian have cut jobs this year, attributing the losses to AI. Telecommunications firm Telstra has also cut jobs from an AI joint venture with Accenture, with some work offshored to India.

More broadly, other firms across corporate Australia have also slashed their domestic headcounts while expanding operations in India, the Philippines and Vietnam, though they did not explicitly mention AI in their announcements. When asked about the Qantas job cuts, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, who was unveiling the response to a recent breach of a government website by an OpenAI agent, said AI "represents an enormous opportunity and a major economic issue." Labour unions have argued that Australian workers were not being replaced by AI, but by lower-paid offshore employees. "Unions are concerned about the risk of companies using AI simply as a cover to cut Australian jobs with no accountability," said Australian Council of Trade Unions Secretary Melissa Donnelly. "From Qantas to the big banks, workers deserve transparency and genuine consultation over decisions that impact their jobs and lives." The Australian Services Union, which represents the affected Qantas workers, accused the airline of "using AI to launder their cuts to Australian jobs." "We expect to see more of this cost cutting and race to the bottom if corporate Australia continues to copy this failed tactic," said Assistant National Secretary Scott Cowen. Senator Barbara Pocock, a member of the Australian Greens party, said on Wednesday that she was concerned to see big companies engaging in "AI washing," using the technology as an excuse to cut jobs. "AI is transforming our workplaces and economy but that's no excuse to let it run rampant," Pocock said in a statement. A Qantas spokesperson said in a statement it would continue to consult with unions and that it was focused on "redeployment opportunities" and support for impacted staff. Qantas did not respond to the concerns around 'AI washing'. Atlassian, WiseTech and Telstra did not immediately respond to requests for comment. TREND TO CONTINUE Further job cuts by companies could pose headaches for Australia's centre-left Labor government, with recent polls showing its approval ratings steadily falling amid high cost-of-living pressures. The central bank has raised interest rates five times so far this year to their highest level in 18 years amid persistent inflation, while the latest data showed the unemployment rate at a five-year high of 4.7 per cent. Uri Gal, a professor at the University of Sydney Business School, said a growing number of companies were blaming job cuts on AI, but "we should therefore be cautious about accepting AI as the primary explanation." "There are real incentives to engage in AI washing," he said. "A company that announces job cuts to reduce costs may face criticism, whereas one that presents the same decision as part of an AI transformation can appear innovative and forward-looking." Gal said the Qantas decision appeared to be due to conventional outsourcing and demonstrated how AI can help justify restructuring before the technology's productivity gains have materialised. "The company has announced that some corporate functions will be transferred to Accenture, primarily in India, and explicitly states that these functions will subsequently be transformed through AI and automation," Gal said. "This raises an obvious question: if AI is making these jobs redundant, why does the work first need to be transferred to another group of employees?" The Reserve Bank of Australia said this week AI had not yet led to widespread job losses, though it noted "tentative signs of adjustment," with job ads weakening in AI-exposed occupations and employment growing more strongly in less affected roles. A government spokesperson said in a statement it expected Australian workers to see the benefits of new technologies and that employers should invest in upskilling them to adopt AI.

Source: Reuters

(Refiles to widen distribution) Nov 11 : Anthropic could see record buying by retail investors in its market debut, potentially surpassing SpaceX and making it one of the biggest single-day retail purchases in history, Vanda Research said in a note on Wednesday. The research firm expects Anthropic's debut to attract about $250 million in net retail buying, based on its analysis of retail activity on listing days and the volume of its pre-IPO perpetual futures traded on Hyperliquid. This would be twice SpaceX's IPO record of $118 million in retail buying. "Judging by pre-IPO perp trading, Anthropic is shaping up to be a record retail IPO," Viraj Patel, global macro strategist at Vanda Research said, in the note.

Pre-IPO perpetual futures are a type of derivative contract which trade on exchanges like Hyperliquid and Coinbase, and allow traders to bet on private companies' valuation. They have no direct link to the underlying shares but are priced with reference to the company's latest disclosed pre-IPO valuation. Only six stocks have topped $250 million in single-day retail buying since 2024, the data firm added. "Anthropic next week could draw the kind of retail buying that we've rarely seen in our data," Vanda said. Anthropic is targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion in its IPO, with shares expected to start trading on the Nasdaq on November 19.

Source: Reuters
